note: Credit and provenance for every asset under ui/board_v2/. Kept in the same machine-readable shape as ui/assets/attribution.json and ui/assets-gothic/attribution.json, so one reader answers the licence question for any tree in this repository.
reproducibility: Two kinds of file live here and they are not equally recoverable. SCRIPT OUTPUT is regenerable: the recipe is recorded per file and was checked rather than quoted, so re-running it reproduces the committed pixels. MODEL OUTPUT is not, because the same prompt does not produce the same picture twice -- which is why every generated master is committed and kept forever, and why anything derived from one records the master it came from.

project-generated.name: Generated by a script in this repository. Nothing traced, photographed or diffused, and no model-generated content is in the file, so there is no upstream licence to honour and nothing to attribute. Where the design was arrived at with an assistant, the file's `design` note says so -- a record of how the decisions were reached, not a rights claim.

openai-generated.name: OpenAI-generated output; rights assigned to the user under the OpenAI Europe Terms of Use. Not CC0, public domain or royalty-free stock

The brief is on record: ui/board_v2/duty_art_lab/prompts/04-open-panorama.md, run with two attached references -- the camera plate, and clerical_master_v03.png as a reference for LINE ONLY.
duty_actions/ordination/masters/ordinati.role: the single wide scene both Ordination action images are cut from, 2172 x 724, and the one the board draws. Kept forever: if the artwork slots change shape the master is re-cropped, never re-generated, because the same prompt does not produce the same picture twice.
duty_actions/ordination/masters/ordinati.notes: master, not shipped. NO DIVIDER. v01 hid the cut behind a masonry pier down the centre line, which worked and read as a contrivance. This one hides it in distance instead: an open churchyard road occupies the middle, and the seam falls in mud and puddles where there is no structure to misalign. Measured, with the caveats that matter. The seam mismatch is 35.0 at the 46th percentile of its own image, which looks poor beside v01's 28.8 at the 8th and is not comparable: that statistic ranks a cut against the quietest place available, and in an open road nowhere is quiet. Inspected at full height instead, the join is not visible. A vertical-alignment check reported a 14 px step; injecting known 4 px and 8 px steps showed the check recovers them on architecture and wanders on bare texture, so that reading is noise and nothing continuous crosses the seam here to step. Chosen on the picture over a sibling generated a minute later, which measured greyer still at 0.149. What is NOT resolved: both groups sit further out towards the edges than the brief asks, so each card carries more open ground on its inner side than v01 did. That was judged by eye; two attempts to measure it failed, edge density being a poor proxy for compositional weight in an engraving where mud hatches as densely as a face.

Ratio 2.0402 against the slot's 2.0380, so `fit: cover` clips 0.4 of a slot pixel.
duty_actions/ordination/ordain/ordinatio.modifications: cut at (0, 101, 1065, 623) by tools/duty_art/crop_duty_master.py --y 101. ADJACENT, NOT OVERLAPPING: the master is cropped once to the band's aspect and split at the gap, so the left window ends at x 1065 and the right begins at x 1107. The 42 px between them is what the board's 15 px gap covers; nothing is shared and nothing is drawn twice. TINT MATCHED to duty_actions/clerical/masters/clerical_master_v03.png at full strength (--match, sha256 a4aed83fe176a67d1f2b561979f269c73bd28b99c5bf566ebe144ee9fdaec82e), so the two duties on the board agree. The transform matches the mean and spread of the two CIELAB chroma channels of the reference's BAND and leaves L* alone: a* +1.61/1.50 -> +2.45/2.22, b* +5.28/2.68 -> +7.80/4.37. Median saturation went 0.176 to 0.247 against the reference's 0.239 while L mean held at 65.2 and its spread at 37.6 -> 37.5. NOT DONE IN THE BRIEF, and that is the finding rather than a shortcut: eleven masters across four briefs came back between 0.15 and 0.27, the scatter inside a single brief being wider than the distance from the greyest to the warmest, so wording steers the average and cannot set the value. No pixel moves, so registration is untouched, and the master is stored unmatched so any crop can be cut again against a different reference.

slotFoldersNote: Which folder under duty_actions/ holds each duty action's pictures. IT CANNOT BE DERIVED and that is why it is written down: Clerical's actionA is `gain_piety` and its actionB `gain_coins`, while Produce's actionA is `gain_wheat` and its actionB `gain_stone` -- so neither alphabetical order nor the action's own name in duty_text.json gives the answer. It lives HERE rather than in duty_text.json because that file is the wording and says so; a folder is a fact about this tree, which is what this file is already about (see assetDirs). A duty with one action has one entry: Taxation and Allocation each have one, and the folders that were left over from before the wording existed -- taxation/action_b and allocation/special_activity -- are stale. ui/board_v2/action_board reads this when a picture lands in a slot that has none yet, and refuses to guess when a slot is missing from it.
nonSlotFoldersNote: Folders under a duty that are NOT one of its actions. Every tool that walks duty_actions/ has to skip them, and until this key existed each one carried its own copy of the word 'masters' -- so when 'seals' appeared, the action board was taught about it and the layout lab was not, and the layout lab quietly drew a 78px wax seal as Clerical's 590x295 action card. One list, read by every walk.
imageSuffixesNote: Extensions an image in this tree may carry, for the walks that look for one. The SHIPPED prints are WebP at quality 90 -- 40 MB of PNG became 7 MB for a worst-case difference of 12 of 255 on one pixel, measured on the seal composited over its tile at the size the board actually inlines. The MASTERS stay PNG: they are the archive, and a lossy archive is not one. Three generators and the tests look for images here, so the list lives in one place rather than four.
defaultProvenance: UNLESS AN ENTRY SAYS OTHERWISE, AN IMAGE IN THIS TREE WAS GENERATED WITH ChatGPT (OpenAI) and carries the openai-generated licence. That is the project's stated default for artwork, not a guess made per file: anything with a different origin -- a third-party icon, a hand-drawn asset, deterministic script output -- has to say so in its own entry, because the default would otherwise quietly mislabel it. A new image added here with no entry at all is a gap, not an implicit default; tests/layout_lab/test_board_v2_attribution.py fails on one.
